History:
• 34-year-old male (Matt Carter) reports 6 weeks of feeling “tired and run-down” with generalized aching (shoulders, back, hips, knees).  
• Symptom onset ≈ mid-February, about two weeks after returning from a U.S. holiday that involved extensive outdoor walking in shorts.  
• Single, non-itchy rash on posterior calf appeared mid/late-February, faded over ~2 weeks; patient shows photograph during consult. Associated mild sore throat and possible low-grade fever at that time.  
• Currently denies fever, cough, dyspnea, chest pain, GI or GU symptoms; no dysphagia, acid reflux, or weight change (notes ↓ appetite & smaller portions).  
• No headaches beyond mild/non-specific; no visual changes, paresthesia, or focal neurologic deficits.  
• Arthralgia/myalgia without visible joint swelling.  
• Functional impact: continues working but with reduced energy and exercise tolerance.  
• Mental health good; no significant stressors reported.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma  
• Hay fever  
• Hospitalizations/ surgeries: not recorded  
• Allergies: not recorded  
Medications:  
• Preventive inhaler (name/dose/route/frequency not documented; used morning and night)  
• OTC antihistamine (name/dose/frequency not documented)  
Social / Lifestyle:  
• Lives with wife; works in health-technology sector.  
• Occasional alcohol; smoking status not recorded.  

Physical Examination:
• Remote video only; no formal examination documented.  
• No visible joint swelling reported by patient.  
• No current cutaneous lesions (rash resolved).  
• General appearance, vitals, cardiopulmonary, abdominal, neurologic exams: not recorded.

Impression:
Fatigue with diffuse myalgia and prior annular calf rash — suspected early Lyme disease.  
Alternate considerations (consistent with transcript):  
1. Post-viral fatigue (e.g., EBV/CMV) — history of sore throat and fatigue.  
2. Hypothyroidism — common cause of fatigue/myalgia; to be screened with TSH.  

Management Plan:
• Order blood panel via support line: CBC, renal & liver profile, thyroid function, inflammatory markers, iron/Vit-D as per standard fatigue work-up, and Lyme serology.  
• Advise patient to attend phlebotomy as soon as possible.  
• Schedule telephone follow-up ~1 week after blood draw to review results.  
• If Lyme serology positive, initiate appropriate antibiotic therapy (e.g., doxycycline)—to be arranged at follow-up.  
• Educated patient on importance of completing blood tests and monitoring for new or worsening symptoms (fever, spreading rash, joint swelling, neurologic changes).  

Patient Summary:
34-year-old man with 6-week history of fatigue and generalized aches following travel-related outdoor exposure; previous transient annular calf rash raises concern for Lyme disease. Blood tests including Lyme serology arranged; telephone review planned once results available.

Key Takeaways:
1. Attend for blood tests promptly and book follow-up call.  
2. Seek care sooner if fevers, new rash, joint swelling, or neurologic symptoms develop.  

Next Steps:
• Patient to arrange blood draw through support line.  
• Clinician to review results at scheduled phone appointment and start antibiotics if Lyme confirmed.  
• Further investigations or referrals (e.g., rheumatology, endocrinology) if initial work-up negative yet symptoms persist.
